result.summary: I treated this as an electrical safety emergency. The EICR is unsatisfactory, with a C2 for a scorched, loose neutral connection in the consumer unit, and the tenant has since reported an odd smell from the fuse box cupboard. Two young children live there. I escalated it to a human as high priority, then booked Sparkwell (the electrician who did the EICR) to come back urgently and make the consumer unit safe, without landlord approval. I emailed the landlord asking her to approve the roughly £620 replacement, gave the tenant safety advice, and put a 12-hour hold on the case for follow-up.
result.situation: Sparkwell Electrical (NICEIC) emailed an unsatisfactory EICR for 8 Kestrel Lane: two C2s (no RCD on the socket circuits; a scorched, loose neutral with heat damage in the consumer unit) and one C3 (no surge protection). They recommend fixing it within 28 days, sooner because of the scorching, at roughly £620. The tenant, Mr Leo Brandt, has two young children and reports an odd smell from the fuse box cupboard. The landlord, Mrs Whitcombe, has no spend limit on file and hasn't been asked for approval yet. The EICR PDF isn't on our file.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 001 records scorching and heat damage at the neutral bar, and event 002 adds a smell from the cupboard. With young children in the home, that counts as electrical danger under the emergency rules. Event 003 shows no spend limit, so the £620 replacement needs Mrs Whitcombe's approval, while the make-safe visit can go ahead as emergency work once escalated as high priority. No past lessons applied.

alternatives_considered.option: Just ask the landlord for approval and wait
alternatives_considered.why_not: A smell plus a scorched neutral is a live risk to a family with children, so waiting isn't safe

alternatives_considered.option: Approve the full £620 replacement as emergency work
alternatives_considered.why_not: The emergency only covers making the unit safe; the permanent replacement can wait a short time for the landlord's decision

alternatives_considered.why_not: I'm not an electrician and the sockets work normally; I gave conditional advice instead and left the decision to the electrician
